title: Model Risk, Explainability and Board Challenge
summary: How to oversee model risk for machine learning and generative AI, what explainability can realistically deliver, and the questions the board should put to management and model validators.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to oversee model risk for machine learning and generative AI, what explainability can realistically deliver, and the questions the board should put to management and model validators.
Learning Objectives: Explain why complex and generative models carry greater model risk
Assess model documentation, validation and monitoring standards
Use a structured question set to probe model risk assurance
Syllabus: Opacity, drift and over-reliance in complex models
Explainability by use case, from credit decisions to trading
Good practice in documentation, independent validation and monitoring
A board question set for approving, extending or retiring a model
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk, audit and technology committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for AI, risk and compliance
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
